Canada's cost of living isn't cooling.

Inflation held at 3.1% year over year in October — the same as September, and still above the Bank of Canada's 2% target, Statistics Canada reported Monday. Groceries actually sped up: 2.0% higher than a year ago, versus 1.7% in September. Slower rent growth is what kept the headline from rising.

Gas looks alarming at 30.9% year over year, but StatCan says that's mostly a base-year effect — pump prices fell 2.5% from September.

My take: a flat headline hides the part that hits the till. Food is re-accelerating while the relief is in rent.

Source: Statistics Canada, Oct. 2026 CPI
